verdict.rationale: Letta agents each have their own private, long-term memory (letta-docs-89), and org-level docs describe collaborators' agents/conversations being 'private by default' with sharing controls that avoid exposing all agent activity org-wide (letta-docs-97, letta-docs-98), which supports per-agent and per-user isolation. However there is no explicit documentation of application-level scoping, no description of retrieval-layer tenant isolation guarantees, and no independent/hands-on verification that memories cannot leak across tenants. Missing for 10: explicit per-application memory scoping, documented isolation architecture/guarantees for retrieval, and independent security validation of tenant separation.
